newsitem.title: USA: Carolina shuts 1,521 MW nuke for hurricane.
newsitem.headline: Carolina shuts 1,521 MW nuke for hurricane.

text.p: Carolina Power & Light Co has shut its 767 megawatt (MW) Brunswick nuclear power unit 1 and was shutting down its 754 MW Brunswick unit 2 due to Hurricane Fran, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.

As of early Thursday, Brunswick 1 was in "hot shutdown" with an "unusual even declared due to Hurricane Fran," while Brunswick 2 had reduced output to 30 percent and was on the way to a shutdown, the NRC said in its daily plant status report.
Hurricane Fran, with 115 mph winds, was expected to hit South Carolina late Thursday. Coastal areas from northern Florida to Virginia have been put on hurricane alert.
The Brunswick nuclear facility is located in Southport, N.C.
"Both units are down from a power production perspective," company spokesman Mac Harris said Thursday morning.
The Brunswick facility will not immediately restart power production once the hurricane has passed, the spokesman said.
"Depending on the damage, we have to do an evaluation of our emergency systems after the storm," Harris said, adding that the evaluation process "typically takes a couple of days."
Carolina Power may have to purchase electricity to make up for lost generation, depending on power demand, he said.
Demand was not expected to be particularily high, however, with clouds and rain contributing to milder weather.
